# 2. PubTator3 Search (Entity highlighting, fallback)
pubtator_results = []
for page in range(1, 10 + 1):
    search_results = pubtator_api_search_papers(
        boolean_query_text='inulin breakfast serum ionized calcium parathyroid hormone acute human',
        relation_query=None,
        page=page,
        max_retries=3,
        max_requests_per_second=3
    )
    if search_results is not None and not search_results.empty:
        pubtator_results.append(search_results)
    else:
        break

if pubtator_results:
    pubtator_df = pd.concat(pubtator_results)
    if "Highlighted_Text" in pubtator_df.columns:
        pubtator_df = pubtator_df.rename(columns={"Highlighted_Text": "Abstract"})
    
    for col in ["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]:
        if col not in pubtator_df.columns:
            pubtator_df[col] = ""
    pubtator_df = pubtator_df[["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]]
    df_list.append(pubtator_df)

# 3. Combine, Deduplicate and Format Clean Output
if df_list:
    final_df = pd.concat(df_list).reset_index(drop=True)
    # Deduplicate by PMID, keeping the first occurrence (which guarantees PubMed relevance is maintained)
    final_df = final_df.drop_duplicates(subset=["PMID"], keep="first")
    
    # Optional: Save to CSV for persistent logging

    print(f"The search results are saved at '/home/data4/xiangyu/BioDSA/workdir/workdir/Inulin_breakfast_calcium_PTH.csv'")
    print(f"Total results found: {len(final_df)}\n")

    # FORMAT FOR LLM: Clean text layout rather than Markdown table

        title = row.get('Title', 'No Title')
        journal = row.get('Journal', 'Unknown')
        year = row.get('Year', 'Unknown')
        abstract = str(row.get('Abstract', 'No Abstract Available'))
        
        # Clean abstract spaces and truncate at 1200 chars to save context window

        if len(abstract) > 1200:

        print(f"PMID: {pmid}")

        print(f"Abstract: {abstract}")
        print("-" * 80)
else:

Title: Addition of inulin to breakfast does not acutely affect serum ionized calcium and parathyroid hormone concentrations.

--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND/AIMS]: The aim of the present study was to investigate the effects of inulin on calcium metabolism. The study consisted of two separate parts both of which had a randomized two-period cross-over design.
[METHODS]: Fifteen young healthy women volunteered to participate in this study. During the first part of the study, cheese containing 210 mg of calcium, either with 15 g of inulin or without any inulin, was ingested at breakfast, and in the second part, 210 mg of calcium as a supplement, either with 15 g inulin or without inulin, was ingested. The whole day's diet was standardized. Before breakfast, and 2, 4, 6 and 8 h after breakfast, a blood sample was taken, and intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), ionized calcium (iCa) and total calcium were measured. Urine was collected throughout the day, and the 8-, 12- and 24-hour calcium excretion was calculated.
[RESULTS]: The iPTH or iCa concentration curves (AUCs) did not differ over 8 h, whether or not inulin was consumed at breakfast. The postload urinary calcium excretion was not affected by the inulin.
[CONCLUSION]: Fifteen grams of inulin in fresh cheese or with a calcium supplement (210 mg Ca) taken at breakfast does not acutely affect the markers of calcium metabolism as opposed to a corresponding breakfast without inulin.
